options.misconception: it appends a zero instead of scaling by the correct factor

questions.explanation: Five hundred cells times five metres is two thousand five hundred metres, and four hundred times five is two thousand metres. Although plausible, "0.5 km by 0.4 km" is a tempting but wrong choice: it divides instead of multiplying. At first glance tempting, "1.0 km by 0.8 km" looks reasonable but does not hold up: it uses cell count as metres. A reasonable-sounding guess, "25 km by 20 km" is a seductive distractor: it appends a zero instead of scaling by the correct factor.

questions.learningObjective: Explain resolution tradeoffs

stimulus.body: Source note: Cell count of a digital elevation model. Finer resolution captures more terrain detail but multiplies cell count and file size, while coarser resolution saves storage but smooths small features.

questions.stem: Using the source note, explain resolution tradeoffs.

answer.exemplar: Finer resolution captures more terrain detail but multiplies cell count and file size, while coarser resolution saves storage but smooths small features.

questions.explanation: Resolution, detail and storage trade off: finer cells improve detail at the cost of larger files. The exemplar grounds the answer in cell count of a digital elevation model rather than restating the question.
questions.hint: Finer cells mean more detail and storage.

questions.subject: HUMAN_GEOGRAPHY
questions.topic: Matching a projection to the job it must do
questions.learningObjective: Explain projection choice for navigation
questions.stem: Biologist Max explains why Mercator is still used for marine navigation despite its area distortion.

answer.exemplar: Mercator preserves angles, so a straight line on the map is a constant-bearing course that a navigator can steer with a compass, which outweighs its area distortion for navigation.

questions.explanation: Angle preservation makes Mercator practical for compass navigation even though areas are distorted. The exemplar grounds the answer in matching a projection to the job it must do rather than restating the question.
questions.hint: Angles matter more than area for navigation.

options.misconception: it is not relevant to the question being asked
it gives a description too general to be the specific answer

questions.explanation: Converting geodetic angles to projected metres is a map projection operation. Although plausible, "Datum transformation" is a tempting but wrong choice: it confuses datum with projection. At first glance tempting, "Legend reading" looks reasonable but does not hold up: it is not relevant to the question being asked. A reasonable-sounding guess, "Scale conversion" is a seductive distractor: it gives a description too general to be the specific answer.
